subtitle: Raw shrimp cured in lime and chile
verso: The shrimp that falls asleep gets carried off by the current.
story: From the coast of Sinaloa: raw shrimp, butterflied and bathed in a blend of lime juice, serrano or chiltepín and cilantro, with cucumber and red onion. It's eaten right away and cold, with tostadas and a cold beer, while the shrimp are still translucent in the middle. The name means chile water.

ingredients.title: The shrimp
items: 1 lb very fresh raw shrimp (about 20 medium), peeled and deveined

ingredients.title: The chile water
items: 3–5 serranos (or 1 tbsp chiltepín, the Sinaloa way)

ingredients.title: On top
items: ½ red onion, very thinly sliced

steps: Butterfly each shrimp: cut along the back almost all the way through and open it flat. Lay them in one layer on a cold plate, salt lightly and refrigerate while you make the chile water.
Blend the lime juice, chiles, cilantro, garlic, salt and water until bright green and smooth.
Pour the chile water over the shrimp so they're covered. Scatter the cucumber and red onion over the top.
Let it sit 5–10 minutes in the fridge, just until the shrimp turn pink outside but stay translucent in the middle. Longer and they toughen.
Serve right away with avocado, tostadas and a little salsa negra.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Aguachile isn't cooked at all: the lime does the work.
tips: Use the freshest shrimp you can find, or shrimp frozen at sea and thawed in the fridge. Raw seafood isn't for pregnant women, small children or anyone with a weak immune system.
Make it right before you eat. Aguachile waits for no one.

variations.name: Aguachile Rojo
variations.subtitle: Red aguachile with chiltepín and chile de árbol
variations.note: The hotter red version, with dried chiles in the chile water.

items: The shrimp, cucumber and red onion from the base

steps: Toast the chiles de árbol a few seconds in a dry pan.
Blend them with the chiltepín, lime juice, garlic, salt and water.
Pour over the butterflied shrimp with the cucumber and onion, wait 5–10 minutes and serve.
